package_info.package_versions: All supported Windows versions prior to August 2021 Patch Tuesday
package_info.why_malicious: The Windows Print Spooler service contained a vulnerability (PrintNightmare) that allowed remote code execution and privilege escalation, enabling attackers to gain SYSTEM-level privileges by connecting to a remote print server under their control. This behavior is not expected from a print service and can be exploited to fully compromise affected systems.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when connecting to a remote print server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker-controlled print server sends a malicious printer driver or DLL to the victim's Print Spooler service, which loads and executes the code with SYSTEM privileges.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Print Spooler service loads a remote printer driver or DLL from an attacker-controlled server, executes arbitrary code as SYSTEM, and enables full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing code from a remote, untrusted server is highly dangerous and not expected in normal print operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, the Print Spooler should only load trusted, signed drivers from approved sources, not arbitrary code from remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise environments may deploy printer drivers from trusted print servers, but these should be authenticated and signed.
key_indicators: Remote loading of unsigned or untrusted DLLs
Execution of code with SYSTEM privileges
Network connections to untrusted print servers

attack_chain.action: Attacker sets up a malicious print server with a crafted printer driver or DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim connects to the malicious print server.

attack_chain.action: Victim's Print Spooler service connects to the attacker's print server and downloads the malicious driver/DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed as SYSTEM.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes with SYSTEM privileges, allowing full system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control of the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Print Spooler service loading DLLs from network shares
Unexpected SYSTEM-level process spawning from spoolsv.exe
Network connections from Print Spooler to untrusted servers
file_indicators: DLLs or drivers loaded from UNC paths (\\attacker\share\malicious.dll)
network_indicators: Outbound SMB or RPC connections to unknown print servers
Connections to non-corporate IPs or domains from Print Spooler
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Print Spooler service activity for attempts to load printer drivers or DLLs from remote, untrusted servers. Alert on spoolsv.exe initiating network connections to unknown hosts, and on SYSTEM-level processes spawned by spoolsv.exe. Review driver installation logs for unsigned or unexpected drivers.
